overview.description: Five Card Stud with pot split between best high hand and best qualifying low hand.

history.origins: Stud poker first appeared in America as early as the 1860s; five card stud was the earliest stud form. Five Card Stud High-Low is a split-pot variant: the pot is divided between the best high hand and the best qualifying low hand, with declaration (high or low) after the final betting round in home games.

nullReasons.evolution: No significant evolutionary changes documented; game remained stable.
nullReasons.cultural: No specific cultural significance beyond general gaming tradition.

setup.dealing: Each player receives one card face down (hole card) and one face up, then three more cards face up, one at a time, with a betting round after each round of cards.

rules.objective: Win the high half of the pot with the best high hand and/or the low half with the best qualifying low hand (e.g. 8-or-better). Low must qualify to win.
rules.gameplay: Deal and betting are the same as in ordinary Five Card Stud. At the showdown the pot is split equally between the highest and lowest hands; the odd chip goes to the high hand if the pot cannot be divided exactly by two. In home games players declare high or low (usually not both) after the final betting round; the best high among declarers and the best low among declarers share the pot.

phases.label: Ante
phases.notes: All players post the ante; then dealer deals one down, one up (second street).

phases.label: Second Street
phases.notes: Betting round after 1 down, 1 up; bring-in or high hand may start.

phases.label: Third Street
phases.notes: Each player receives one card face up; then betting.

phases.label: Fourth Street
phases.notes: Fourth card face up; then betting.

phases.label: Fifth Street
phases.notes: Fifth card face up; final betting round.

phases.label: Declare
phases.notes: Players declare high or low (e.g. chips in fist); usually cannot declare both; simultaneous reveal.

phases.label: Showdown
phases.notes: Reveal five cards; best high and best qualifying low determine winners.

phases.label: Award Pot
phases.notes: Pot split between high and low; odd chip to high; low must qualify.

ante.description: Post the required ante into the pot before any cards are dealt.
ante.constraints: Mandatory at start of hand; amount agreed (e.g. small fraction of small bet).

deal.reason: Deal is performed by the dealer; not a player action.

fold.description: Forfeit the hand and drop out of the current pot; no further action in the hand.
fold.constraints: Legal during any betting round when it is your turn to act.

check.description: Decline to bet when no bet has been made in the current round; stay in the hand.
check.constraints: Legal only when no player has bet in the current betting round.

call.description: Match the current bet to stay in the hand.
call.constraints: Legal when at least one player has bet in the current round and you have not yet matched.

bet.description: Place a bet (small or big bet per street rules); opens or reopens the betting.
bet.constraints: Legal when no bet has been made this round, or when completing from bring-in; amount depends on street and limit.

raise.description: Increase the current bet; subsequent players must call the new amount or fold.
raise.constraints: Legal when a bet has been made; maximum three raises per round; raise size small or big per street.

declare.description: Declare high or low (e.g. chips in fist); revealed simultaneously; usually cannot declare both in Five Card Stud High-Low.
declare.constraints: After fifth street betting; required before showdown when playing with declaration.

reveal_hand.description: Show all five cards; best high and best qualifying low (if any) determine winners.
reveal_hand.constraints: At showdown; cards speak; winners split pot by declaration.

award_pot.description: Pot split equally between best high hand and best qualifying low; odd chip to high; no qualifying low means high wins entire pot.

play_card.reason: Five Card Stud is a deal-and-bet game; players do not play cards to a trick, they bet and reveal at showdown.

engine.deckDescription: One full deck of 52 cards using French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) and standard ranks from ace through king, with no jokers.
engine.suitDescription: French suits: hearts (cœurs), diamonds (carreaux), clubs (trèfles), and spades (piques). Each suit has thirteen cards from ace through king.
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranking for a 52-card deck: ace (high or low by context), king, queen, jack, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2. Thirteen cards per suit.
engine.dealPattern: 1 down, then 4 up (one card at a time with betting after each up card).
